messages.content:
You are AutoSkill's offline DOCUMENT skill extractor.
Task: expand ONE planned reusable asset from one document window into one complete executable skill.
Output ONLY strict JSON parseable by json.loads.

Decision policy:
- Expand only the provided planned asset; do not add a second asset.
- Treat the result as a reusable skill contract with routing cues, guardrails, execution steps, and an output or handoff guarantee.
- Be conservative. If the candidate is not sufficiently supported by the excerpt, return {"skill": null}.
- Keep the asset single-goal and reusable.

Rules:
1) Treat the candidate name, candidate description, candidate use_when, candidate do_not_use_when, and candidate success_artifact as the scope anchor.
2) Do not rename the asset into a different capability unless the excerpt clearly requires a minor normalization.
3) Do not expand beyond the planned scope or merge in unrelated steps from the same window.
4) Keep macro_protocol, session_skill, micro_skill, safety_rule, and knowledge_reference separate.
5) Translate candidate use_when into triggers/applicable_signals, candidate do_not_use_when into contraindications/constraints, and candidate success_artifact into output_contract whenever the excerpt supports them.
6) Keep hard constraints, safety rules, therapist moves, sequence, and output checks when directly supported.
7) Preserve caller-facing boundaries: the skill should make it clear when a caller should invoke it, when a caller should avoid it, and what the caller gets back.
8) De-identify: remove names, IDs, dates, local paths, one-off payload details.
9) If the excerpt only partially supports the candidate, keep the skill minimal instead of hallucinating details.
10) Include 1-3 short therapist-response examples only when the source directly supports them.


Taxonomy guidance:
Domain type is externally provided as `board game endgame rules`.
Do not infer or output domain_type.
Return asset_type using ONLY the internal base types: macro_protocol | session_skill | micro_skill | safety_rule | knowledge_reference.
Domain-specific labels and aliases:
- macro_protocol -> macro_protocol: Cross-phase or multi-stage reusable protocol. (aliases: protocol, macro)
- workflow_skill -> session_skill: One reusable workflow-level skill or session-sized scaffold. (aliases: workflow_skill, session, skill)
- micro_skill -> micro_skill: One tightly scoped move or mini-sequence. (aliases: micro, micro_intervention)
- safety_rule -> safety_rule: Safety, escalation, compliance, or guardrail rule. (aliases: safety, risk_rule, policy)
- knowledge_reference -> knowledge_reference: Reference-style knowledge asset with limited direct execution content. (aliases: knowledge, reference)
Configured hierarchy nodes:
Return asset_node_id when the excerpt strongly maps to one configured node; otherwise omit it.
- family_root -> macro_protocol (level=0, role=root, parent=null) [总技能 / Family Root] synthesized-only
- macro_skill -> macro_protocol (level=1, role=parent, parent=family_root) [一级技能 / First-Level Skill] default
- workflow_skill -> session_skill (level=2, role=parent, parent=macro_skill) [二级技能 / Second-Level Skill] default
- micro_skill_node -> micro_skill (level=3, role=leaf, parent=workflow_skill) [微技能 / Micro Skill] default
- safety_module -> safety_rule (level=1, role=parent, parent=family_root) [一级技能 / Safety Module]
- safety_rule_node -> safety_rule (level=2, role=leaf, parent=safety_module) [二级技能 / Safety Skill] default
- knowledge_reference_node -> knowledge_reference (level=1, role=leaf, parent=family_root) [一级技能 / Reference Skill] default
Return schema: {"skill": {...}} or {"skill": null}.
Skill fields:
- name, description, prompt, triggers, tags
- asset_type (macro_protocol|session_skill|micro_skill|safety_rule|knowledge_reference)
- optional asset_node_id (must be one configured taxonomy node id when present)
- granularity (macro|session|micro), objective
- domain, task_family, method_family, stage
- applicable_signals, intervention_moves, contraindications
- workflow_steps, constraints, cautions, output_contract
- examples: array of 1-3 short objects like {input, output, notes?}
- relation_type (support|constraint|conflict|case_variant), risk_class (low|medium|high)
- confidence (0.0-1.0)
- optional resources/files (safe relative paths under scripts/, references/, assets/; concise content only)

Field boundaries:
- description: what the asset does and when to use it, not evidence recap.
- prompt: only execution guidance for the asset itself; do not repeat article metadata or long quotations.
- triggers and applicable_signals: routing cues and entry conditions that tell a caller when to invoke this skill.
- contraindications and constraints: when not to use the skill, or what conditions must hold before and during execution.
- output_contract: the completion artifact, handoff, or observable success condition for downstream callers.
- task_family/method_family/stage should use compact reusable labels, not broad domain labels such as 心理咨询 / psychology.
- asset_node_id, when present, must be a configured taxonomy node id; otherwise omit it.
- examples should be omitted unless the source directly supports concrete example language.

Language:
- Use one dominant language from the source text for ALL textual fields.
- If dominant language is unclear, return {"skill": null}.

JSON validity:
- Escape newlines as \n and escape quotes correctly.
- No Markdown wrapper, output raw JSON only.

Can you give us a summary of some of the differences and then help us get started. We're a family rang"}, "excerpt": "4. POSSIBLY: Support 1 Conservation objective You have 4 Conservation Achievement markers, each of which you can use to support 1 Conservation objective. You may not support a single objective more than once. The Conservation objectives show you which icons you need to collect to support them. Each Achievement marker indicates the minimum number of icons of a type that you must have in your zoo to support an objective (e.g. you may also use the 4-icon Achievement marker if you have 5 icons for an objective). They also show you how many points the placed Achievement marker is worth at the end of the game. In this step, you may support exactly 1 Conservation objective that you have not yet supported. Count the number of icons in your zoo that match the objective you want to support. You may increase that number by returning Conservation markers you have collected during the game to the supply. Each Conservation marker you return increases the number of icons by 1. However, you must have at least 1 matching icon in your zoo to support a Conservation objective. You are therefore not allowed to replace all icons with Conservation markers when supporting a Conservation objective. Then place an unused Achievement marker with the matching number of icons face down on the Conservation board, below the Conservation objective you're supporting, on the space of your color. 
EXAMPLE: You have 3 bird icons in your zoo (A), but you want to use the best possible Conservation Achievement marker that will earn you the most points. You therefore also discard the 2 Conservation markers you have collected. You then place your 5-icon Conservation Achievement marker on the space of your color underneath the Bird Conservation objective (B). It is worth 14 points at the end of the game. Any further bird icons that you place in your zoo will no longer help you with Conservation objectives. Conservation objectives (random) 5-icon achievement. 
5 POSSIBLY: Upgrade Action cards You have 4 Upgrade markers, each of which you can use to upgrade any 1 of your Action cards. You can therefore upgrade all 4 Action cards during the course of the game if you meet all the conditions (you may use several at once): You have supported at least 1 Conservation objective. You have at least 2 Projects in your zoo. You have at least 3 connected tiles of a single habitat (mountain, forest, water) in your zoo. You have at least 4 different Animal class icons in your zoo. Carry out the following steps for each of your previously unused Upgrade markers whose condition you have met (which might be multiple markers, one right after the other): 1. Choose 1 of your Action cards that has not yet been upgraded. 2. Flip it from side I (upward pointing arrow on the left) to side II (upward pointing arrow on the right). This increases the strength of future actions and gives you more options. 3. Then turn the used Upgrade marker face down. You cannot use it again. 
EXAMPLE: After you have played the Tree House in step 3, you have 3 connected tiles with a forest icon in your zoo (A). You have now met the condition of the "3 connected tiles of a single habitat" Upgrade marker and flip it over (B). This allows you to upgrade 1 of your Action cards and you decide to flip the Water Animals action card over to side II (C)-This increases the strength of this action by 1 for the rest of the game. For example, if you were to use the Water Animals action on your next turn, it would have a strength of 4 (instead of 3 from before the upgrade) and you could play up to 2 water animals (instead of just 1). 
ADMINISTRATION: Keep to the tile limit, replenish the display, and check whether the game ends 
TILE LIMIT: If you now have more than 6 tiles in your hand, you must discard tiles until you have exactly 6 tiles left. You may have more than 6 tiles in your hand during your turn, but not at the end of your turn. 
REPLENISH THE DISPLAY: First, if necessary, move the tiles already in the display to the next lower empty number on the Display board until there are no more gaps between the tiles. Then place a face-up tile from the pile next to each empty number on the board, so that the display once again contains 6 tiles.
CHECK WHETHER THE GAME ENDS: Then check whether at least 1 of the conditions for the end of the game has been met (see next section). If none of the end conditions have been met, the next player in clockwise order takes their turn. 
EXAMPLE - REPLENISHING THE DISPLAY: At the start of your turn, you took the tile from position 2 into your hand. With the Projects action, you were then allowed to take any tile and took the tile in position 5. At the end of your turn, you first move down the tiles in positions 3, 4 and 6. Then you reveal 2 new tiles from the pile and place them in the now empty positions 5 and 6.  
---END OF THE GAME AND FINAL SCORING 
The end of the game is triggered when at least 1 of the 3 possible end conditions is met at the end of a turn. 
The 3 end conditions - 1 You have supported 4 Conservation objectives, so all 4 of your Conservation Achievement markers are on the Conservation board. 2 You covered your Zoo map completely, so there is not a single empty space left on it. 3 The pile of face-down tiles is empty. If, at the end of your turn, you've met condition 1 and/or 2 take the 10-point End-of-game marker. Then everyone else gets 1 more turn (excluding you). After that, move on to the final scoring. If the pile of face-down tiles is empty after you have triggered the end of the game, shuffle all the discarded tiles to form a new pile. □ If you also meet condition 1 and/or 2 on your last turn, after someone else has triggered the end of the game, take a 5-point End-of-game marker. If you meet condition 3 before one of you meets condition 1 or 2, the game ends immediately after your turn. Directly proceed to the final scoring. 
Final scoring Add up: • the points on the tiles in your zoo. Some tiles have a fixed point value. For other tiles, the value depends on how many icons of a specific type you have adjacent to that tile or anywhere in your zoo. First, count the points of your Animals (yellow), then the Buildings (blue), the Projects (purple), and the Open Areas. • the points on your Conservation Achievement markers on the Conservation board (i.e. the achievements with which you supported objectives). • 2 points for each Pouch marker and each remaining Conservation marker in your possession. • The points (10 or 5) on your End-of-game marker, if you have one. • Solo mode only: 5 points for each face-down Solo marker. The player with the most points wins the game. In the event of a tie, the tied player with more Animals in their zoo wins.
